quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Lane ends.
Two-way traffic.
Side road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you not to enter. It is posted at the end of one-way streets. When you see this sign, stop and turn around. You are going the wrong way.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Never make a sudden turn to catch your exit. If you miss it, keep driving and take the next exit.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Passing may be unsafe and illegal on hills where you cannot see ahead. Use caution when approaching a large truck from behind.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: As speed increases, the risk of death increases. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is unlikely. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make unsafe moves to pass you.

questions.question: Your gas pedal sticks while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off your ignition, taking care not to lock the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition, taking care not to lock the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the gas pedal sticks, your vehicle will keep going fast. Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move safely off the road.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect your driving?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It gives you false confidence.
It impairs your thinking.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment and balance. It also weakens your vision and ability to judge distance. Alcohol makes you feel overconfident, which leads to poor decisions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They warn you of hazards ahead. This sign means pedestrians may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: When should you signal before turning or changing lanes?

options.text: Only if other traffic is present.
It is a good habit and the law requires it.
Only during the maneuver, not before.
Not necessary if you do it slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a good habit and the law requires it.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. You must signal at least 100 feet before you move. When pulling away from a curb, signal to inform other drivers of your intentions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that the road may be slippery when wet. Drive carefully in these conditions.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Before backing, always check behind your vehicle. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other cars.
Drive slower than other cars.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Always drive at the same speed as traffic around you, but stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Slow down and go carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: When the road is wet, slow down.
The road ahead has many curves.
More traffic is coming.
A steep hill is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road is wet, slow down.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, reduce your speed, avoid sudden braking or turning, and stay farther away from the car in front of you.

questions.question: You can pass another vehicle if the lane divider is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Narrow bridge.
One-way.
No parking anytime.
No turn on red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Narrow bridge.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that a bridge ahead has narrow lanes.

questions.question: Alcohol:

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces your driving skills. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: When you drive faster:

options.text: You can see more around you.
You can see less around you.
It is easier to see traffic crossing your path.
It does not change what you can see.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see less around you.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the less you can see around you. As you speed up, you must be extra careful to watch for hazards.

questions.question: To change lanes you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, turn on your signal and check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one is moving into the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Stops the effects of alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. It may help you stay awake, but it cannot make you sober.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Traffic is merging from the right.
Highway curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is entering the road from the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign means an intersection is coming. Watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back on the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently brake and slowly steer back to the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake and slowly steer back to the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels off the pavement and gently slow down using the brakes. When your speed is safe, turn the steering wheel slowly to return to the pavement. Do not sharply turn the wheel.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go slowly and wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than traffic.
Turn on hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the ramp to speed up to the same speed as freeway traffic. This helps you merge safely. Vehicles entering must give way to vehicles already on the freeway.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Don't worry about how many tracks are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop. A train may be using the tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Road work ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the road will curve to the right and then to the left. Slow down to safely handle these curves.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting an expressway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles, motorcycles, bicycles, in bad weather, in heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Steer straight and slow down by releasing the gas pedal.
Keep your speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to warn traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight and slow down by releasing the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Release the gas pedal slowly. Do not brake until you have control. Once in control, brake gently and move to a safe spot.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive in the right lane only.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems ahead without sudden braking. This helps prevent crashes from cars behind you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are allowed on the upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge has only one-way traffic.
Only one car can cross the bridge at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns drivers about hazards. It tells you the upcoming bridge may be too narrow to safely meet or pass a truck. Drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield ahead.
Railroad crossing.
Low shoulder.
Deer crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare you for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign tells you that a yield sign is ahead. Be ready to stop and let other drivers and pedestrians go first.

questions.question: When driving past a parked car on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.
Speed up.
Slam on your brakes.
Assume that the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume that the driver will open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: When passing a parked car, assume the driver may open the door suddenly. Drive slowly and carefully near parked vehicles.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, move to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you will need to use more force to turn the wheel. Slow down and move off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cattle crossing.
Prepare to stop.
Detour ahead.
Winding road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cattle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare you for upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns that cattle may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
Always stop before crossing the tracks.
Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train at the crossing.
questions.explanation: Always be prepared to yield to trains at railroad crossings. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side of the tracks. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle may stall.

questions.question: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down. If possible, change lanes to stay away from the emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.
Speed up to quickly pass the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If possible, change lanes to stay away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down well below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: When approaching a green traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving, unless vehicles or pedestrians are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles still in the intersection. You may drive through, but go at a speed that lets you slow down or stop if the light changes.

questions.question: When a school bus stops with its stop arm extended, drivers should:

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
Honk their horn before passing the bus on its left.
Continue driving when they think most kids are done exiting the bus.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.
questions.explanation: When a school bus stops with its stop arm out, you must come to a complete stop. Do not proceed until the stop arm is withdrawn.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
Decreasing your chances of an accident.
Causing you to fall asleep at the wheel.
Making you more aware of others around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reducing your ability to focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions hurt your driving. If you are worried, excited, angry, afraid, or sad, you may not drive well. Stress makes it hard to concentrate. Wait to drive until you feel calm and ready.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.
You have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a "Keep right" sign. It tells you that a traffic island, median, or barrier is ahead. Drive to the right of it.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop if needed.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop and wait for all vehicles and pedestrians to pass before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn right or go straight.
Turn left only.
Do not enter.
Two-way left turn lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right or go straight.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers they can turn right or drive straight ahead from this lane at an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Do not speed.
A traffic light is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic light is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a traffic light ahead.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do before moving your car?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children you are moving.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
Tell the children to stay away from the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to check that the way is clear.
questions.explanation: When backing up, look through your back window. Do not rely only on mirrors, especially with children nearby. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing up.

questions.question: Which is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Drive at the same speed through the curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Gradually increase your speed as you exit. Speeding into a curve makes your vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: When an aggressive driver is near you, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Tailgate them to retaliate.
Show them you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between you and an aggressive driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: You notice a problem with your vehicle that could affect safe driving. What should you do?

options.text: Fix it as soon as possible.
Fix it when you have money.
Drive slowly.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix it as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any problem that affects safe driving must be fixed right away before you drive the vehicle.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should NOT:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Look for other drivers moving into your lane.
Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police about the road ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors for traffic behind you. Use your turn signal. Look for other drivers also moving into your lane. Never use your phone while driving.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must yield?

options.text: Either one
The vehicle on the left
The vehicle on the right
Neither

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: At any intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, along with fog lights if you have them. High beams bounce off fog and reflect back into your eyes, making it harder to see.
